# Explanation
##  No Target Variable(There is no Prediction)
- goal: the main goal of unsupervised machine learning is to reduce dimension(dimension reduction using pca) and classify the variables into groups or clusters using k-means clustering

# load the dataset
```{r}
data<-read_excel("PCA data.xlsx")
head(data)
```


# confirm names
```{r}
names(data)

```

# check data structure
```{r}
str(data)
```
# check number of rows and columns
```{r}
dim(data)
cat("NO of rows:",nrow(data),"\n","No of columns:",ncol(data))
```
# summary statistics
```{r}
summary(data)
```

# check missing values and dupliccates
## check missing values
```{r}
sum(is.na(data))
colSums((is.na(data)))
```

# check for duplicated rows
```{r}
sum(duplicated(data))
```
# examine the correlation
```{r}
# correlation matric
correlation<-cor(data)
# display correlation values
round(correlation, 2)
# visualize correlation
corrplot(
  correlation,
  method="color",
  type="upper",
  addCoef.col="yellowgreen"
)
```

## why check correlation?
- purpose: to seee which variables are related,. PCA is particulalry useful when variables share overlapping information.


# standardize the variable
```{r}
data_scaled<-scale(data)

# check the means
cat("The mean of standardized data.:\n")
round(colMeans(data_scaled), 2)
# check standardization deviation
cat("The sd of standardized data.:\n")
round(apply(data_scaled, 2, sd, 2))
```

# perform pca
```{r}
pca_results<-prcomp(
  data,
  center=TRUE,
  scale.=TRUE,
)
summary(pca_results)
```

# component loading
```{r}
pca_results$rotation
head(pca_results$x)
```

# PURPOSE: 
- THIS CREATES NEW VARIABLES 
```{r}
#  Eigenvalues (variance of each PC)
eigenvalues <- pca_results$sdev^2

#  % variance explained
variance   <- eigenvalues / sum(eigenvalues) * 100

# 4. Cumulative % variance
cumulative <- cumsum(variance)

#  Build the table
results <- data.frame(
  component           = paste0("pc", seq_along(eigenvalues)),
  Eigenvalue          = round(eigenvalues, 3),
  Variance_percentage = round(variance, 2),
  Cumulative_percent  = round(cumulative, 2)
)
print(results)
```


# draw the  scree plot
```{r}
plot(
  eigenvalues,
  type="b",
  pch=19,
  xlab=" Principal Component",
  ylab="Eigenvalues",
  main="PCA Scree plot"
)
abline(h=1, lty=2, col="red",lwd=1)
```


# select number of components
```{r}
# using cumulative variance
number_compopnents<-which(cumulative>=80)[1]
cat("components retained:", number_compopnents,"\n")
cat("cummulative variance explained:", 
    round(cumulative[number_compopnents],2),"%")
```

# interplet component loadings
```{r}
loadings<-pca_results$rotation[
  , 1:number_compopnents,
  drop=FALSE
]
round(loadings*100, 3)
```

# Attain the main goal of pca
## reduce dataset from 10 original variables to the number of components selected
# extract the retained compobnents
```{r}
reduced_data<-as.data.frame(
  pca_results$x[
    ,1:number_compopnents,
    drop=FALSE
  ]
)
head(reduced_data)
```


# check new dimension of data set]
```{r}
dim(reduced_data)
```

# save the reduced data set
```{r}
library(writexl)
write.csv(
  reduced_data,
  "PCA_Reduced_Datase.xlsx",
  row.names=FALSE
)
```
